title: Psalm 11 (Septuagint) = Psalm 12 (KJV)
description: Psalm 11 in the Septuagint numbering (Psalm 12 in the KJV). Both the manuscript page scan AND the Greek text are taken directly from Codex Sinaiticus (4th century AD) via the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). The Greek transcription preserves the actual uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra abbreviations, and lectional marks of the manuscript. Library folio: 90. English translation verbatim from the King James Version (1611, public domain) via bible-api.com.
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library, with the manuscript text drawn directly from the same source as the scan:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio of Codex Sinaiticus containing this passage, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Library folio reference: 90.
  2. Original text: The verbatim transcription of the Sinaiticus manuscript from the Codex Sinaiticus Project, preserving uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra (e.g. ⟨θϲ⟩ = θεός), and scribal marks. Nomina sacra are shown in angle brackets to indicate the manuscript's sacred-name abbreviations.
  3. English translation: The King James Version (1611), retrieved verbatim from the public-domain bible-api.com endpoint.

Numbering: Codex Sinaiticus follows the Septuagint Psalter, in which this is Psalm 11. In the Hebrew and King James numbering the same psalm is Psalm 12. Greek verse numbers follow the Septuagint, which counts the superscription as verse 1; English verse numbers follow the KJV, so they run 1 behind the Greek. The Greek and English in each section are the same words of the same psalm.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ειϲ το τελοϲ ϋπερ τηϲ ογδοηϲ ψαλμοϲ τω δαυειδ <sup>2</sup>ϲωϲον με κε οτι εκλελοιπεν οϲιοϲ οτι ωλιγωθηϲαν αι αληθειαι απο > των υιων των ανθρωπων <sup>3</sup>ματαια ελαληϲαν εκαϲτοϲ προϲ τον πληϲιον αυτου χειλη δολια εν καρδια και εν καρδια ελαληϲαν <sup>4</sup>εξολεθρευϲαι κϲ παντα τα χειλη τα δολια και γλωϲϲαν μεγαλορημονα <sup>5</sup>τουϲ ειπονταϲ την γλωϲϲαν ημων μεγαλυνουμεν τα χειλη ημων παρ ημων εϲτιν τιϲ ημων κϲ εϲτιν
translation.text:
<sup>1</sup>Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men. <sup>2</sup>They speak vanity every one with his neighbour:
with flattering lips
and with a double heart do they speak. <sup>3</sup>The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips,
and the tongue that speaketh proud things: <sup>4</sup>Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips
are
 our own: who
is lord over us?

translation.text:
<sup>5</sup>For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set
him in safety
from him that
 puffeth at him. <sup>6</sup>The words of the LORD
are pure words:
as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. <sup>7</sup>Thou shalt keep them, O LORD, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever. <sup>8</sup>The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted.
